ArchitectureNotes.objective: Deliver a horizontally scalable, CQRS-based payment processing microservice in MIF where Reader (read-only query path) and Writer (command gateway path) are independently deployable, with Worker sagas processing commands via MQ and persisting to MongoDB.
ArchitectureNotes.non-goal: This plan does not cover IdentityService integration (delegated auth), SWIFT network adapters, or real-time FX.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-1: Read-write consistency: MongoDB eventual consistency window may show stale states on Reader queries immediately after saga completion.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-2: Partition key per saga: Wolverine saga ordering relies on partition key = correlationId. Incorrect key derivation breaks ordering.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-3: Idempotency at saga boundaries: replay of a partially-processed saga must skip already-completed steps.

contract.purpose: Shared DTOs, events, commands used across Reader, Writer, and Worker projects.

type-PaymentRequestDto.PURPOSE: Inbound payment request schema for Writer API

type-PaymentCommand.PURPOSE: Payment processing command for Worker saga

contract.purpose: Read-only query API: receives payment status queries, validates via FluentValidation, queries MongoDB directly (no MQ, no saga involvement).

fn-QueryMongoDB.PURPOSE: Direct read-only MongoDB query (no saga involved)

contract.purpose: Command gateway API: receives payment commands, validates, routes to MQ via Dapr pub/sub (asynchronous, does not wait for saga completion). Returns 202 Accepted with correlationId.

export-PostPayment.PURPOSE: POST /api/payments — accept payment command, route to MQ

fn-PublishToMQ.PURPOSE: Publish PaymentCommand to Dapr pub/sub with partition key = correlationId

contract.purpose: Saga processor subscribed to MQ: receives PaymentCommand, executes Wolverine saga state machine (validate → enrich → settle → notify), persists saga state and payment document to MongoDB. Implements idempotency and compensation.

export-ProcessPaymentHandler.PURPOSE: Wolverine message handler: receives PaymentCommand from MQ, starts PaySaga

class-PaySaga.PURPOSE: Wolverine saga: Validate → Enrich → Settle → Notify (with compensation on failure)

fn-CheckIdempotency.PURPOSE: Idempotency check against MongoDB ledger before each saga step

fn-Compensate.PURPOSE: Compensation logic: reverse settlement, release reserved funds, update saga state to Failed

fn-PersistPaymentDocument.PURPOSE: Persist or update payment document in MongoDB after saga step

contract.purpose: MongoDB data access layer: payment documents, saga state persistence, idempotency ledger, transactional session support.

export-IPaymentDocumentRepository.PURPOSE: Repository for payment document CRUD (used by Reader for queries, Worker for persistence)

export-ISagaStateRepository.PURPOSE: Repository for saga state CRUD with transactions

export-IIdempotencyLedger.PURPOSE: Interface for idempotency key tracking to prevent duplicate saga steps

DF-COMMAND-PATH.NAME: Command Path (Write)
DF-COMMAND-PATH.step-1: Writer API receives PaymentRequestDto, validates via FluentValidation, assigns correlationId.
DF-COMMAND-PATH.step-2: Writer publishes PaymentCommand to Dapr pub/sub with partitionKey = correlationId (MQ partitioning).
DF-COMMAND-PATH.step-3: Writer returns 202 Accepted + correlationId to caller (fire-and-forget).
DF-COMMAND-PATH.step-4: Worker (subscribed to MQ partition) receives PaymentCommand, starts PaySaga.
DF-COMMAND-PATH.step-5: Saga: validate → enrich → settle → notify. Each step checks idempotency ledger, persists state + payment document to MongoDB.
DF-COMMAND-PATH.step-6: On saga completion: PaymentSettled event emitted, payment document status = Settled in MongoDB.

DF-QUERY-PATH.NAME: Query Path (Read)
DF-QUERY-PATH.step-1: Reader API receives query with correlationId, validates via FluentValidation.
DF-QUERY-PATH.step-2: Reader queries MongoDB directly (no MQ, no saga involvement) for the payment document.
DF-QUERY-PATH.step-3: Reader returns 200 + payment document or 404 if not found.

DF-SAGA-LIFECYCLE.NAME: Saga Lifecycle with Compensation
DF-SAGA-LIFECYCLE.step-1: Worker handler starts PaySaga with correlationId from partition key.
DF-SAGA-LIFECYCLE.step-2: Saga step 1: ValidatePayment — check idempotency, validate DTO, check duplicate payment id.
DF-SAGA-LIFECYCLE.step-3: Saga step 2: EnrichPayment — enrich with reference data from MongoDB.
DF-SAGA-LIFECYCLE.step-4: Saga step 3: SettlePayment — mark as settled, persist final state.
DF-SAGA-LIFECYCLE.step-5: On any step failure: trigger compensation → revert settlement, release reserved funds, update saga state = Failed.
DF-SAGA-LIFECYCLE.evidence: [Worker][PaySaga][BLOCK_COMPENSATE] emitted on failure; no BLOCK_MARK_SETTLED after compensate; saga state persisted with status=Failed.

Phase-1.name: Foundation
Phase-1.goal: Establish solution structure, shared contracts, persistence layer, and unit test harness.

solution.name: PaymentServices
solution.step-1: Create PaymentServices.sln + PaymentService.Shared project with all DTOs/events/commands.
solution.step-2: Implement PaymentService.Persistence: repositories, transactional sessions, idempotency ledger.
solution.step-3: Integration tests: Testcontainers.MongoDB, transactional writes, idempotency key uniqueness.

Phase-2.name: Reader-and-Writer
Phase-2.goal: Query path (Reader) and command gateway (Writer) working end-to-end up to MQ publish.

solution.name: PaymentServices
solution.step-1: Implement PaymentService.Api.ReaderService: GET endpoints, FluentValidation, MongoDB direct query (no MQ).
solution.step-2: Implement PaymentService.Api.WriterService: POST endpoints, FluentValidation, Dapr pub/sub publish with partition key.
solution.step-3: Integration test: Reader queries MongoDB, Reader/Writer endpoints respond correctly, Writer→MQ publish verified.

Phase-3.name: Worker-Saga
Phase-3.goal: Core saga processing: Wolverine saga state machine with validation, enrichment, settlement, and DLQ failure handling.

solution.name: PaymentServices
solution.step-1: Implement PaymentService.WorkerService: PaySaga (validate→enrich→settle→notify), idempotency checks, MongoDB saga persistence.
solution.step-2: DLQ handler: on saga failure at any step, publish FailedPaymentEvent to DLQ with full context (original input, failed step, error).
solution.step-3: Saga integration tests: happy path, DLQ on validation failure, idempotency replay, concurrent saga isolation.

Phase-4.name: Deployment-and-Scale
Phase-4.goal: K8s manifests, Dapr component configs, GitOps pipeline, and throughput validation under load.

solution.name: PaymentServices
solution.step-1: K8s manifests: Reader/Writer/Worker Deployments, Dapr pub/sub Component, MongoDB StatefulSet, DLQ topic.
solution.step-2: GitOps pipeline: centralized repo integration, automated deploy on merge to main.
solution.step-3: Load test: 1000 msg/s sustained on write path, 1000 queries/s on read path, verify partition distribution, measure p99 latency, validate zero message loss, DLQ processing.

ExecutionPolicy.worker-owns: Only module source files and module-local tests inside the approved write scope.
ExecutionPolicy.replan-trigger: Missing dependency, contradictory contract, or unclear third-party surface.
ExecutionPolicy.checkpoint-requirement: Every step must leave assumptions, commands run, evidence, and next action.
